# Config — `lasius.toml`
<!-- generated by gen-config-docs.py — edit the struct doc comments,
     not this file -->

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | `string` | required | Org (or user) whose non-archived repos are managed. |
| `provider` | `ProviderKind` | optional | Git forge that owns repo discovery. Unknown values are a config error — there is no silent fallback. |
| `repos_dir` | `string` | optional | Directory under the workspace root that holds clones. |
| `workspace_file` | `string` | optional | VS Code workspace file name; defaults to `{org}.code-workspace`. |
| `exclude` | `list` | optional | Glob patterns (`*`, `?`) of repo names to skip during discovery. |
| `include_private` | `bool` | optional | Include private repos in discovery (requires `gh` auth with access). |
| `checks` | `CheckConfig` | optional | `[checks]` — conformance engine toggles. |
| `policy` | `Policy` | optional | `[policy]` — org conventions enforced by `lasius check`. |

## `[checks]` table

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `list` | optional | Check ids (kebab-case) to skip entirely. |
| `severity` | `map` | optional | Per-check severity overrides, e.g. `{ "worktree-health" = "warn" }`. |

## `[policy]` table

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `require_worktrees` | `list` | optional | Worktree names every clone must have (e.g. `["project", "docs"]`). |
| `require_files` | `list` | optional | Files every clone must contain (e.g. `["AGENTS.md"]`). |
| `remote_must_match_org` | `bool` | optional | Treat a clone whose `origin` doesn't match `org/&lt;name&gt;` as an error (default: warn). |

## Example

```toml
org = "9aia"
repos_dir = "repos"
exclude = ["workspace"]

[checks]
# disabled = ["<check-id>"]
severity = { "<check-id>" = "warn" }

[policy]
require_worktrees = ["project", "docs"]
require_files = ["AGENTS.md"]
```

## Constraints

- `lasius.toml` is discovered by walking ancestors from the cwd
  (or `--root <dir>`); every field except `org` has a default.
- `provider` is a closed set — unknown values are a config error;
  there is no silent fallback.
- `exclude` entries are glob patterns (`*`, `?`) matched against
  repo names.
- Secret material never lives here.
